title: Can't unpair DualShock 3 controllers
line: DualShock 3 controllers now show up in the Bluetooth applet and settings, where they can be forgotten, instead of in the Add Device window.
explanation: DualShock 3 controllers are paired over a USB cable, and BlueZ's sixaxis plugin then marks them Trusted but never Paired. The applet and KCM only list devices that are paired or connected, so a powered-off controller was hidden there, while the pairing wizard only hides paired devices and kept offering it as a new one. The change counts trusted devices as known ones: the applet and KCM list them (with Forget), and the wizard and the Bigscreen unpaired list skip them.

commits.message:
applet, wizard: list trusted but unpaired devices as known devices

DualShock 3 controllers are set up over USB, so BlueZ marks them trusted
but never paired and they only showed up in the pairing wizard. Treat
trusted devices like paired ones, so they can be found and forgotten.

BUG: 519548

media.caption: Before: with a trusted, unpaired DualShock 3 known to BlueZ, the Bluetooth applet lists no devices.
Before: the same controller is offered as a new device in Add Bluetooth Device.
After: the applet lists the controller (Paired: No, Trusted: Yes) with a Forget action.
After: Add Bluetooth Device no longer offers the already set up controller.

review.text: Treating BlueZ's TrustedRole alongside PairedRole in both the applet/KCM proxy model and the pairing wizard cleanly resolves the DualShock 3 cable-pairing issue (and helps other trusted-but-unpaired HID devices). The diff is minimal, updates Bigscreen's unpaired filter consistently so devices aren't duplicated, and the before/after screenshots and Forget verification confirm the fix without regressing ordinary unpaired devices.

reviews.text: Treating BlueZ's TrustedRole alongside PairedRole in both the applet/KCM proxy model and the pairing wizard cleanly resolves the DualShock 3 cable-pairing issue (and helps other trusted-but-unpaired HID devices). The diff is minimal, updates Bigscreen's unpaired filter consistently so devices aren't duplicated, and the before/after screenshots and Forget verification confirm the fix without regressing ordinary unpaired devices.

Right diagnosis and the right repo: BlueZ's sixaxis plugin (and bluedevil's own wizard, which only trusts and connects DS3 pads through the NULL-PIN path) leaves DS3 controllers Trusted but not Paired, while bluedevil's filters only treat Paired as known. Counting Trusted as known in the shared applet/KCM DevicesProxyModel and hiding it from the wizard and the Bigscreen unpaired list is a small, consistent fix, and the dbusmock before/after shots show the controller moving from the wizard to the applet with a working Forget. The only side effect is that a DS3 whose first connect from the wizard fails stays trusted and shows up as known rather than re-offered, which is acceptable since it can be forgotten. The KCM view wasn't opened, but it uses the same proxy model.
